title: Hourly to Annual Pay: How Your Salary Compares to the NBA Salary Cap
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay using a 38-hour week and 52-week year. See how your salary stacks up against the NBA salary cap and learn about minimum wage, casual loading,
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours (38 × 52).

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

faqs.q: What is the current National Minimum Wage in Australia?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and apply to award/agreement-free employees.

faqs.q: How is superannuation and tax calculated on my annual pay?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your gross pay at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Tax is deducted using the 2026–27 resident tax rates: tax-free up to $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy of 2% also applies. Our calculator provides an estimate only.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your Pay

Whether you're negotiating a salary, budgeting for the year, or just curious how your hourly wage translates to a yearly figure, converting your pay is straightforward. The basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, that means multiplying your hourly rate by 1,976 (38 × 52). This gives you the gross amount before tax, super, and any deductions.

### Why 38 Hours?

The 38-hour week is the standard ordinary hours for full-time employees under many awards and the National Minimum Wage. The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage based on a 38-hour week. If you work part-time or casual, your weekly hours may differ, so adjust accordingly.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for 38 hours, your weekly pay is $1,004.90, so your fortnightly pay is $2,009.80. This can help with budgeting and comparing to salary offers.

## Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

Australia has a complex pay system. The **National Minimum Wage** is the baseline for award/agreement-free employees. However, most workers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, which include minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates.

**Casual loading** is an extra 25% on top of the base rate for casual employees, compensating for lack of paid leave. For example, the casual National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check the casual loading box to add 25% to your base rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; always start with the base hourly rate.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your gross pay. This is not deducted from your salary. The maximum contribution base for the 2026–27 year is $270,830. So if your annual pay exceeds that, super is capped. For most workers, super adds a significant boost to your total remuneration.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates for residents in 2026–27:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator estimates your net pay after tax and Medicare, using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds (as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed).

## How Does Your Pay Compare?

To put your annual salary in perspective, consider the NBA salary cap for the 2026–27 season. While the exact figure fluctuates, it's in the range of $150–$160 million USD per team. That's a far cry from the average Australian full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week (ABS May 2026), which equates to about $108,352 per year. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page has more details.

Your own annual pay, calculated from your hourly rate, might be closer to the National Minimum Wage ($52,254 per year) or above the average if you're in a high-paying industry. Use our [reference tables](/data) to see how different hourly rates translate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Using the Hourly to Annual Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) is the home page. Simply enter your base hourly rate, and we'll show your annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay. If you're a casual, check the casual loading box to add 25% on top. The calculator uses the 38-hour week assumption but you can adjust hours if needed. For award-specific rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

Whether you're comparing your salary to the NBA salary cap or just planning your budget, understanding your annual pay is the first step.
